title: Sum of even numbers
description:
Write `SumOfEvens.Calculate(int[] numbers)` that returns the **sum of the even numbers** in the array.

- `[1, 2, 3, 4]` → `6`
- `[]` → `0`
- Negative even numbers count too: `[-2, 3]` → `-2`

Use a `foreach` loop and the `%` operator. No LINQ for this one!

title: FizzBuzz
description:
Write `FizzBuzz.Generate(int n)` that returns a `List<string>` for numbers **1 to n**:

- multiple of 3 → `"Fizz"`, multiple of 5 → `"Buzz"`, multiple of both → `"FizzBuzz"`
- otherwise the number as text (`"1"`, `"2"`…)

If `n <= 0`, return an empty list. Classic interview warm-up — write it without looking anything up.

title: Price with VAT (decimal)
description:
Irish VAT is **23%**. Write `PriceCalculator.Total(decimal unitPrice, int quantity, decimal vatRate)` that returns the total **including VAT, rounded to 2 decimals** (use `Math.Round(value, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero)`).

- `Total(10m, 3, 0.23m)` → `36.90m`
- Throw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` if `quantity < 0` or `unitPrice < 0`.

💡 Why `decimal` and not `double` for money? Think about it — it will be asked in the teach-back.

title: Min and max (tuples)
description:
Write `MinMax.Find(int[] numbers)` that returns a **tuple** `(int Min, int Max)` in **one pass** over the array (one loop, no `Min()`/`Max()`/sorting).

- `[3, 9, -2, 7]` → `(-2, 9)`
- Throw `ArgumentException` if the array is empty, `ArgumentNullException` if it is null.

title: Reverse words
description:
Write `ReverseWords.Reverse(string sentence)` that reverses the **order of the words**.

- `"hello world"` → `"world hello"`
- Extra spaces are removed: `"  I   love .NET "` → `".NET love I"`
- Empty or whitespace-only → `""`

Hint: `Split` with `StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries`, then `string.Join`.

title: Valid palindrome
description:
Write `Palindrome.IsPalindrome(string text)`: return `true` if the text reads the same forwards and backwards, **ignoring case and anything that is not a letter or digit**.

- `"A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"` → `true`
- `"race a car"` → `false`
- `""` → `true`

Try the **two-pointer** technique (one index from the start, one from the end) instead of building a reversed string. `char.IsLetterOrDigit` and `char.ToLowerInvariant` help.

title: Two Sum
description:
The most famous interview question. Write `TwoSum.Find(int[] nums, int target)` that returns the **indices** `[i, j]` (with `i < j`) of the two numbers that add up to `target`. Exactly one solution exists.

- `nums = [2, 7, 11, 15], target = 9` → `[0, 1]`
- `nums = [3, 2, 4], target = 6` → `[1, 2]`

1. First write the simple **O(n²)** version with two loops.
2. Then make it **O(n)** with a `Dictionary<int, int>` (value → index). The tests include a big array, so the O(n²) version may be slow.

title: struct vs class in practice
description:
Two types are already declared: `struct MoneyStruct` and `class WalletClass`. Implement:

1. `MoneyStruct.Add(decimal amount)` → adds to `Amount`.
2. `WalletClass.Deposit(decimal amount)` → adds to `Balance`.
3. `Demo.CopyStructThenChange()` → create a `MoneyStruct` with 10, copy it into a second variable, `Add(5)` on the **copy**, and return the **original** amount.
4. `Demo.CopyClassThenChange()` → same with `WalletClass` (start at 10, copy, `Deposit(5)` on the copy) and return the **original** balance.

Before running the tests, **predict** both results and write them in a comment. Were you right? This is exactly the class vs struct interview question.

title: Bank account (encapsulation)
description:
Implement a `BankAccount` that **protects its own state**:

- Constructor `BankAccount(string owner)`; `Owner` is read-only, `Balance` starts at 0 and **cannot be set from outside**.
- `Deposit(decimal amount)`: amount must be > 0, else `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`.
- `Withdraw(decimal amount)`: amount must be > 0 (`ArgumentOutOfRangeException`) and ≤ Balance, else `InvalidOperationException("Insufficient funds")`.
- `History` returns the list of operations as read-only (`IReadOnlyList<decimal>`): deposits positive, withdrawals negative.

Think: why is `public decimal Balance { get; set; }` a bad idea here?

title: Shapes (inheritance & polymorphism)
description:
Create a small shape hierarchy:

- `abstract class Shape` with `public abstract double Area();` and a `virtual string Describe()` returning `"Shape with area X"` (X rounded to 2 decimals, e.g. `"Shape with area 12.57"`).
- `Circle(double radius)`, `Rectangle(double width, double height)`, `Square(double side)` (**Square inherits from Rectangle**).
- `Circle` **overrides** `Describe()` → `"Circle r=2"`.
- `ShapeTools.TotalArea(IEnumerable<Shape> shapes)` sums all areas — this is **polymorphism**: it doesn't know which shapes it gets.
- Invalid sizes (≤ 0) throw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`.

title: Notifications (interfaces)
description:
Program **to an interface**, not an implementation:

- `INotifier` with `string Channel { get; }` and `bool Send(string to, string message)`.
- `EmailNotifier` (`Channel = "email"`) and `SmsNotifier` (`Channel = "sms"`): `Send` returns `true`, but **SMS fails** (returns `false`) if the message is longer than 160 characters.
- `NotificationService(IEnumerable<INotifier> notifiers)` with `int NotifyAll(string to, string message)` that sends through **every** notifier and returns how many succeeded.

The tests also use a **fake notifier**. This is why interfaces make code testable, and it leads directly to dependency injection in week 4.
